title: The brief carries how hard the node is
description:
The score is set where the work is actually understood — `write_brief`, not `propose`. A brief already names real files and real functions; a node title does not.

Add `complexity` to `Brief` in `packages/schema/src/brief.ts`, an integer on a 1–10 scale beside `approach` and `acceptance`. Raise `SCHEMA_VERSION` to 6 in `packages/schema/src/project.ts` and add the step to `MIGRATIONS` in `packages/core/src/migrate.ts` — a migration reads raw JSON rather than a parsed record, and the four before it are the pattern. What that migration does to a brief written before the field existed is the decision this node binds.

Carry the field through `writeBrief` in `packages/core/src/brief.ts` and the `write_brief` tool in `packages/mcp/`. Add one line to step 2 of `plugins/skills/brief/SKILL.md` telling the agent to score the node and justify the number in the approach, then run `pnpm plugins`. Nothing here reads the score — that is the dispatch node — so this one is finished when a brief round-trips with it and a v5 board opens without complaint.

brief.approach:
The score lives on the brief, where the work is understood. Five files, one generated set, in this order:

**1. Schema — `packages/schema/src/brief.ts`.** Add `complexity: z.int().min(1).max(10).nullable()` to `Brief`, beside `approach`. `null` is a brief written before the score existed (the decision this node binds: no score → no tier → `dispatch.host`). No `.default()` on it — node records are migrated, not defaulted (contrast `Run` in `run.ts`, which is a local file). Tests in `brief.test.ts`: `null` parses, 0 and 11 and 7.5 do not.

**2. Version — `packages/schema/src/project.ts`.** `SCHEMA_VERSION = 6`.

**3. Migration — `packages/core/src/migrate.ts`.** One entry `{ to: 6, node }` after the `to: 5` step, in the voice of the ones above it: a node with `brief: null` is left alone; one with a brief gets `{ complexity: null, ...brief }` — spread order leaves a value already there alone, as `to: 2` does. Two tests in `migrate.test.ts`: a v5 node with a brief arrives with `complexity: null` and still parses; a v5 node with no brief is untouched. The existing "board written by an older SOBER is brought forward" tests keep passing with the new number.

**4. Writers.**
- `packages/core/src/decide.ts` `writeBrief`: keep every existing caller compiling — the six integration tests and the CLI pass `{ approach, acceptance }`. Type the parameter as `Omit<Brief, 'approval' | 'complexity'> & { complexity?: number | null }` and write `complexity: brief.complexity ?? null`.
- `packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts` `write_brief`: add `complexity: z.int().min(1).max(10)` to `inputSchema` — **required** there, because the tool is the agent scoring the node, and a tool that lets it skip the score is a board that never gets one. Pass it through to `writeBrief`.
- `packages/cli/src/work.ts` `brief --write` and `packages/server/src/routes.ts` use `Brief.omit({ approval: true })`, so they take the field as the schema defines it; nothing to change unless typecheck says so.
- `packages/core/src/brief.ts` (the rendered skeleton `sober brief <node>` prints): one line under the title, `Complexity: 7 / 10`, or `Complexity: not scored` — so the number a human approves is on the page they approve.

**5. Skill — `plugins/skills/brief/SKILL.md`**, step 2, one more bullet: score the node 1–10 for how hard it is for one agent in one run in this repository — files touched, how much has to be understood first, how easy it is to check — and say in one sentence of the approach why that number. Then `pnpm plugins`, and commit the generated `packages/*/skills/brief/SKILL.md` files with it; `test/integration/plugin.test.ts` is the drift check.

Nothing reads the score yet — that is `the-dispatch-picks-the-model-from-the-sc-c9n8`. The dashboard panel (`apps/dashboard/src/panel/Panel.tsx:107`) renders `approach` only; leave it, the surfaces node `0o4s` owns what a screen shows.

acceptance.proves: a brief round-trips with the score and refuses one outside 1–10; a v5 board arrives at v6 with `complexity: null` on every brief and no other field touched
the version moved, so an older SOBER refuses this board instead of dropping the field on its next write
the four generated brief skills match `plugins/skills/brief/SKILL.md` after `pnpm plugins` — the scoring instruction reaches every host
the tool takes the score, the skill asks for it, and the rendered brief shows it
every `writeBrief` caller — six integration tests, the CLI, the server route — still compiles against the new `Brief`
